newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close off highs in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close off highs in active trade.

text.p: Italian shares closed off day's highs in active trading on Thursday, knocked back by late news of lower first half profits from insurer Generali and especially Credito Italiano bank, traders said.

"The tone of the market remains positive but Credito's half year net profit of 70.5 billion lire against 90.8 billion pulled the share price down," one said. Credito closed 1.88 percent down at 1,668 lire.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 1.09 percent up at 9,849 after a high of 9,898 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed 1.17 percent up at 14,807 after a 14,903 high.
Generali, posting first half pre-tax profit of 516 billion against 584.6 billion, ended off 31,800 lire highs at 31,650 lire, 1.81 percent up.
Telecoms performed well, with mobile phone operator TIM up 3.34 percent at 3,222 lire, Telecom Italia up 3.06 percent at 3,270 and their holding Stet up 2.47 percent at 5,070.
The market was helped by strong bonds and the lira and trading was estimated at around 700 billion lire, a touch down on Wednesday.
"But despite recent days' gains, uncertainty over the 1997 budget is weighing on the market," one Milan trader said.
Troubled high-tech group Olivetti posted a modest gain of 0.67 percent to 526.3 lire but Carlo De Benedetti's industrial holding CIR put on 5.88 percent to 675.2 lire.

Tyre and cable-maker Pirelli was down 0.26 percent at 2,666 lire ahead of first half results which came in after the close showing first consolidate net profit up at 206 billion lire against a previous 115 billion.
Energy group ENI, with a second tranche of shares to be sold next month, ended 0.91 percent up at 7,428 lire.
